Replay

Compact recent facts

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Compact recent facts reduce header overhead when the authority copies recent recorded occurrence batches onto the unreliable channel. Protocol-7 feature 4096 permits envelope kind 27, Recent_Facts_Compact. It replaces repeated inner packet envelopes and connection scopes with one shared header. The reliable fact stream, every-other-tick bundle cadence, four-tick coverage, canonical events, recipient filtering and normal admission remain intact. No previous packet or decoding baseline is required.

The outer envelope retains the epoch, content and newest tick. Its fingerprint is the logical Facts schema fingerprint, binding the event schema as well as the connection header. The body is:

  1. Generation u64, serial u64, entry count u8, using the existing canonical Recent_Facts_Header codec. Entry count is 1–4.
  2. Each entry: age u8, event count u16 little-endian, then that many complete canonical occurrences. Age is 0–3; the fact tick is outer tick minus age.

Entry ticks must be positive and strictly increasing. Event counts remain bounded by WIRE_EVENTS. Canonical decoding, exact length, occurrence epoch/tick, duplicate identity and retained-fact conflict checks all run before any entry is admitted. Validated entries then use the same receiver as reliable facts. History exhaustion and presentation errors retain their normal explicit handling.

Packets remain bounded by the smaller of the host limit, the recipient’s advertised part_bytes, and SNAPSHOT_PART_BYTES. An entry that does not fit is skipped; its reliable delivery and request-based repair are unchanged. Smaller headers can let more complete entries fit. Event payloads are not truncated. Four empty entries occupy 81 bytes rather than 389.

The client offers support after each Welcome through the existing feature exchange. The server sends compact bundles only for an offered capability and current generation/serial. No acknowledgment is needed for this downstream-only format: the offering client already knows how to receive it. Older clients receive kind 19; older servers ignore the new offer and continue sending kind 19. Restored peer state resets the server's selection and requires a fresh offer.

Client.compact_recent_facts_enabled defaults to true. Disable it before negotiation to retain kind 19. Server.compact_recent_facts_disabled provides a server opt-out. Godot's Session_Options.disable_compact_recent_facts applies both through open and resume. Changing these flags during an admitted session is not supported.

Stats.compact_recent_facts counts successfully sent compact bundles. Stats.recent_fact_bytes_saved counts header savings for those entries relative to their kind-19 representation; that hypothetical full bundle might exceed the packet limit when compact headers allow more events to fit. Existing redundant_facts and redundant_fact_bytes include either encoding. These statistics do not include transport framing or retransmissions.
